analysis:
The only changed file is docs/architecture/inference.md, a documentation file. No patch hunks were supplied, only base lines 829-1195 and head lines 1-400, so I could not compare the two versions. The head excerpt covers only the first 400 lines and the base excerpt only the tail, so the changed regions are likely not covered.

I found no code, control or deployment change in the visible text. The visible head text (the 2026-10-16 date stamp, GLM5Next boundary, calibration and startup-warmup sections) describes request-local measurements and native ownership. It makes no new claim about encryption, attestation, authorization, TTL or the cache, and it does not contradict the T-041 SSD prefix-cache posture (30-minute TTL, HMAC lookup tags, coordinator-authored cacheSalt). Visible base statements on MiMo media and decode accounting, in-memory video assets, and coordinator-serving channels are also consistent with the threat model. The video-asset statement says payloads are not written to disk, which matches T-050. The coordinator-channel statement says the provider encrypts SSE frames back over the coordinator connection, which matches T-008.

The next pass should check any prose change in the prefix-cache, SSD or TTL claims against T-041 and SEC-035, including raising the TTL beyond 30 minutes or weakening account isolation. It should also check any changed claim about encryption on the coordinator-serving channel (T-008) or about disk writes of media (T-050). I did not review the unseen middle and later head regions, so this is a coverage limit rather than evidence of safety.
